title: Computation of the alternating product of the Chern classes of the exterior powers of a locally free module
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a locally free module E of rank r the lemma computes the alternating product of the total Chern classes of its exterior powers: the product over n = 0, ..., r of c(wedge^n E)^{(-1)^n} equals 1 - (r-1)! c_r(E) plus higher terms (statement lines 12499-12509). The proof applies the splitting principle to replace the computation by one in the polynomial ring on the Chern roots x_1, ..., x_r, writes c(wedge^n E) as the product over increasing multi-indices i_1 < ... < i_n of (1 + x_{i_1} + ... + x_{i_n}), and then takes the logarithm of the alternating product to obtain a double sum over p and n with the sign (-1)^{p+n}/p (proof lines 12512-12527). The key observation is the identity of the last display, namely that the corresponding sum with 1/p! equals the product of (1 - e^{-x_i}); the author notes explicitly that the minus sign in front must be kept, and deduces that the lowest nonzero degree of the alternating product is r, with the value predicted in the statement (proof lines 12528-12538). Setting up the logarithmic computation and matching the coefficients of the resulting exponential product is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
